'''Niels Keiding''' (14 May 1944 – 3 March 2022<ref name="jrssa_2022">{{cite journal |last=Kragh Andersen|first=Per|year=2022|title=Obituary: Niels Keiding |url=https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/rssa.12850 |journal= [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series A]] |volume=185 |issue=3 |pages= 1456–1457|doi=10.1111/rssa.12850 |s2cid=248093578 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>) was a Danish [[biostatistician]].

==Biography==
=== Education ===
Keiding studied at the [[University of Copenhagen]], graduating with a [[Candidate (degree)|cand.stat.]] degree (roughly equivalent to a [[Master's degree]] in other countries) under supervisor [[Anders Hald]] in 1968.<ref name="jrssa_2022"/>

=== Teaching and professional experience ===
At the [[University of Copenhagen]], Keiding successively held assistant, associate
and, from 1984, full professor positions, the latter in the section of Biostatistics within the
Faculty of Health Sciences. In 1971 he was one of the founders of the {{ill|Danish Society of Theoretical Statistics|dk|Dansk Selskab for Teoretisk Statistik}} (DSTS), serving as its secretary from 1971–1975. The [[Scandinavian Journal of Statistics]] was founded in 1974, with DSTS being one of its four societal board members.<ref>[https://www.jstor.org/publisher/bfsjs Board of the Foundation of the Scandinavian Journal of Statistics]</ref> He was head of the Biostatistics section until three years prior to retirement.
In 2014 he became Professor emeritus at the section.
<ref name="jrssa_2022"/>

=== Research and development===

Keiding's research spanned several fields. In [[demography]], he published on [[nonparametric statistics|nonparametric inference]] for the [[Lexis diagram]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/abs/10.1098/rsta.1990.0128|title=Statistical inference in the Lexis diagram|first=Niels|last=Keiding|journal=[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A]]|year=1990|volume=332|issue=1627|pages=487–509 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1990.0128 |bibcode=1990RSPTA.332..487K |s2cid=122677661 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> With coauthors he contributed to event history analysis, including to models where only partial information is available. He applied the latter to time-to-pregnancy (TTP), which
is the timespan from the start of when a couple tries to become pregnant until they succeed.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://smm.sagepub.com/cgi/content/abstract/11/2/91|title=Multi-state models for event history analysis |last1=Kragh Andersen|first1=Per|last2=Keiding|first2=Niels|journal=[[Statistical Methods in Medical Research]]|year=2002|volume=11|issue=2|pages=91–115|doi=10.1191/0962280202SM276ra |pmid=12040698 |s2cid=2726913 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In a survey with coauthors, he clarified how [[survival analysis]] is used to analyze TTP.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Keiding|first1=Niels|last2= Højbjerg Hansen|first2=Oluf K.|last3=Nørbo Sørensen|first3=Ditte |last4=Slama|first4=Rémy|title=The current duration approach to estimating time to pregnancy  |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1467-9469.2012.00798.x |journal=[[Scandinavian Journal of Statistics]]|volume=39|issue=2|pages=185–204|year=2012|doi=10.1111/j.1467-9469.2012.00798.x |s2cid=33370189 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

His book, ''Statistical models based on counting processes'', written jointly with Per Kragh Andersen, Ørnulf Borgan, and [[Richard D. Gill]], has been cited extensively in the medical literature<ref>{{cite journal|title=Multi-state models for the analysis of time-to-event data|last1=Meira-Machado|first1=Luís|last2=de Uña-Álvarez|first2=Jacobo|last3=Cadarso-Suárez|first3=Carmen|last4=Kragh Andersen|first4=Per|journal=[[Statistical Methods in Medical Research]]|volume=18|issue=2|pages=195–222|year=2009|doi=10.1177/0962280208092301 |pmid=18562394 |pmc=2692556 }}</ref> and been lauded for its "lucid" exposition of theoretical and practical aspects. Its survey of [[statistical model]]s based on [[counting process]]es has been called "thorough".<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://zbmath.org/0769.62061|title=Review of "Statistical models based on counting processes"|last=Valkeila|first=Esko|work=[[ZbMATH Open]]|series=Springer Ser. Stat. |date=n.d.|publisher=Springer |isbn=9780387978727 |access-date=24 January 2023}}</ref>

Keiding co-authored an influential meta-analysis, known as Carlsen study after the name of the first author, that showed a significant [[Male infertility crisis|decline in human sperm count and volume]] from 1938 to 1990.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2017/07/25/health/sperm-counts-declining-study/index.html|title=Sperm counts of Western men plummeting, analysis finds|first=Susan|last=Scutti|work=[[CNN]]|date=25 July 2017|access-date=20 January 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Carlsen|first1=Elizabeth|last2=Giwercman|first2=Alexander|last3=Keiding|first3=Niels|last4=Skakkebaek|first4=Niels E.|date=12 September 1992|title=Evidence for decreasing quality of semen during past 50 years|journal=[[BMJ (Clinical Research Ed.)]]|volume=305|issue=6854|pages=609–613|doi=10.1136/bmj.305.6854.609|issn=0959-8138|pmc=1883354|pmid=1393072}}</ref>

He also wrote about the history of the use of [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingales]] in survival analysis (with coauthors),<ref>{{cite book|last1=Aalen|first1=Odd O.|authorlink1=Odd Aalen|last2=Kragh Andersen|first2=Per|last3=Borgan|first3=Ørnulf|last4=Gill|first4=Richard D.|authorlink4=Richard D. Gill|last5=Keiding|first5=Niels|title=The Splendors and Miseries of Martingales |series=Trends in the History of Science |editor-last1=Mazliak |editor-first1=Laurent |editor-last2=Shafer |editor-first2=Glenn|date=2022 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-05988-9 |location=Cham |publisher=Springer |chapter=Martingales in Survival Analysis |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-05988-9_13|pages=295–320|doi=10.1007/978-3-031-05988-9_13 |isbn=978-3-031-05987-2|arxiv=1003.0188|s2cid=5060138 }}</ref> and of demography,<ref>{{cite journal|title=The method of expected number of deaths, 1786-1886-1986|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1403267|first=Niels|last=Keiding|journal=[[International Statistical Review]]|year=1987|volume=55|number=1|pages=1–20|doi=10.2307/1403267 |jstor=1403267|pmid=12179583 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> in particular age-period-cohort analysis in the 19th century.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/apc/files/analyzing_age-period-cohort_data-_a_review_and_critique1.pdf|title=Analyzing Age-Period-Cohort data: a review and critique|last1=Fosse|first1=Ethan|last2=Winship|first2=Christopher|authorlink2=Christopher Winship|journal=[[Annual Review of Sociology]]|year=2019|volume=45|pages=467–492|doi=10.1146/annurev-soc-073018-022616 |s2cid=182417675 }}</ref>

=== Work for international scientific organisations ===
Keiding served as treasurer of the [[Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability]] (1981–1987), chairman of the board of the [[Scandinavian Journal of Statistics]] (1988–1991), and president (1992–1993) of the [[Biometric Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=
https://www.statsoc.org.au/resources/Documents/Newsletters/1993-%20March%20SSA%20News%2062.pdf|title=XVIth International Biometric Conference on |work=[[Statistical Society of Australia Newsletter]]|date=31 March 1993|issue=62|issn=0314-6820}}</ref>
He was a member of the Research Section Committee of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] (1999–2003), and member of council and several ad hoc committees in the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] (IMS) and the [[International Statistical Institute]] (ISI). He was president-elect of the ISI in 2003–2005,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25472665|title=Roles of statistics in the life sciences|last=Keiding|first=Niels|journal=[[International Statistical Review]]|year=2004|volume=73|issue=2|pages= 255–258|doi=10.1111/j.1751-5823.2005.tb00288.x |jstor=25472665|s2cid=120170693 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and president in 2005–2007.<ref name="jrssa_2022"/>

==Honours and awards==
His honours and awards include:
{{div col|colwidth=35em}}
* 1978 Elected membership of the [[International Statistical Institute]]
* 1987 Fellow of [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]
* 2005 Elected membership as Foreign Member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Utenlandske medlemmer|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26861|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715102608/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26861|archive-date=15 July 2007|access-date=1 September 2024|website=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no}}</ref>
* 2005 Honorary Doctor at [[University of Bordeaux]]
* 2008 Honorary Life Member, [[International Biometric Society]]
* 2011 Member, [[Academia Europaea]]
{{div col end}}
